title: coordination.md and monitoring.md say the same about whether an open ask waits announce.needs_you_after_min minutes before it enters the needs-you line
goal: kb/_self/coordination.md's description of announce.needs_you_after_min says what kbmon does with an open ask to the operator, the same as kb/_self/monitoring.md and _tools/mon_needs.py do (an ask is named at once, the setting delays an undecided overlap only)

run:
import re, sys
t = open('kb/_self/coordination.md', encoding='utf-8').read()
line = [l for l in t.splitlines() if l.startswith('- **`announce.needs_you_after_min`**')]
bad = bool(line) and bool(re.search(r'open (question|ask)', line[0]))
print('setting line', line[:1] and line[0][:140], '| says an open question waits', bad)
sys.exit(1 if bad or not line else 0)

notes: Review gap (S2) of SP-d6gbc3tq: coordination.md:173 says the setting delays any open question, monitoring.md:98 and mon_needs.py apply it to an undecided overlap only (ST-n5vf55qk gate g1: asks are named with no delay). If the operator wants the delay for asks, change the code and gate g1 instead.
